claims.statement: Identification of the sitter as Ginevra de' Benci rests on the juniper (ginepro) pun and on the early sources that mention a portrait of her by Leonardo; the NGA states the commissioner and the painting's early history are not known.

sources.cite: National Gallery of Art, 10 surprising facts about Ginevra de' Benci. Read via web search result summary in this session; the page itself could not be fetched (host blocked), so the wording must be rechecked on the page.

claims.value: Liechtenstein collection by 1733; sold to NGA 1967
claims.statement: The NGA provenance states the painting was presumably bought in Florence by Prince Johann Adam Andreas I of Liechtenstein before 1712, was certainly in the Liechtenstein collection by 1733 (a red wax seal of 1733 on the reverse), was listed as Lucas Cranach in the Liechtenstein catalogue of 1780, and was sold by Prince Franz Josef II to the National Gallery of Art in 1967 (Ailsa Mellon Bruce Fund).
